input.message:
I built the tools and numbered the record in two commits on `main`. Nothing is pushed.

**Commits**
- `a74f5a2b7`: `tools/record.py`, `tools/record-number.py`, `tools/test_record.py`, the `facts-extract.py` change, and `.record.lock` in `explorations/.gitignore`.
- `a88e52bf7`: the numbering. Both record files and both history files, `PLAN.md`, `review-queue.md`, `climb-batch-workflow.md`, the kit's `key.md`, `fill.py` (finds `{FACTS n}` by `F-n`), two sentences of the kit's README, and a 3-line fix to `record-number.py --verify`.
- The usage section is in `record.py`'s header, so it went into `a74f5a2b7`. There is no `tools/README.md`.

**Commands and queries as built**
- PROV is `--from PATH#HEADING` (repeatable), `--commit HASH`, `--by WHO`, `--note WHY`. A write needs `--from` or `--note`; the tool stamps the UTC time and derives the kind.
- `record.py add F|P --section TITLE FILE PROV`: numbers the entry (highest number ever used plus one) and puts it at the end of its section.
- `record.py set N [FILE] [--section TITLE] PROV`: rewrites or moves an entry. A retitle refreshes the quoted words in every pointer to it, in both files, and lists the entries it changed in one line of the retitled entry's block.
- `record.py merge N --into M [FILE] PROV`: N goes, M is rewritten or kept, and pointers to N become pointers to M.
- `record.py remove N PROV`: refused while any pointer to N remains, naming each.
- `record.py apply FILE PROV`: checked against the state it would leave, then all or none. The file holds:
  - entry lines, and `F-?n` placeholders for new entries under a `##`/`###` heading;
  - `move F-n to SECTION`, `remove F-n` and `merge F-n into F-m` lines;
  - one indented `from:/commit:/by:/note:` line per item.
- `record.py check [--base COMMIT] [--summary]`: fails on form, one-line, number, history, pointer, pointer-words and base-line; reports oversized entries, untitled entries and report sections that don't resolve.
- `record-number.py [--write] [--verify BASE] [--list FILE]`: the one-off numbering and its three checks.
- `facts-extract.sh 'F-87'`, `'F-87+'` and `'history:F-87'`. Title queries and `positions:TITLE` fall back to former titles and say the entry was retitled or merged. `title_of` skips the number.

**Tests**
- `test_record.py`: 16 tests, all pass, run before and after the numbering commit.
- `test_ledger.py`: 10 of its 13 tests fail. The same 10 fail with HEAD's own `facts-extract.py`, so this was already broken: the tests expect the ledger as it was before its sections were renamed ("Grammar and lexing") and before row 83 and the bare-pipe rows were repaired. I left them alone.

**Numbering figures**
- **Entries numbered:** 308, F-7 to F-219 (195) and P-7 to P-145 (113).
- **FACTS history:** 572 of 959 old texts linked to 166 entries (487 by exact title, 85 by the same first 60 characters), giving 37 former titles.
- **POSITIONS history:** 62 of 328 texts linked to 39 entries, with no former titles.
- **Pointers converted inside the record:** 207 in all.

  | From | To | Converted |
  |---|---|---|
  | FACTS | FACTS | 104 |
  | FACTS | POSITIONS | 70 |
  | POSITIONS | FACTS | 27 |
  | POSITIONS | POSITIONS | 6 |
- **Pointers converted in the live documents:** 161 (`PLAN.md` 58, `review-queue.md` 51, `climb-batch-workflow.md` 29, `key.md` 23).
- **Ambiguous:** none inside the record. Four citations in the live documents stay by title:
  - `PLAN.md` "The specification allows arithmetic in a size and does not say when two size expressions are the same type": this entry was retitled before tonight, so the citation was already stale.
  - `PLAN.md` "The territory map": a FACTS section, not an entry.
  - `key.md` "by root cause", twice: the words are inside F-54's title, not its opening.
- **Checks before the commit:**
  - `record-number.py --verify a74f5a2b7` passes. Each entry is its old line with the number added and its pointers converted. Of 1,881 title citations in 672 tracked files, 1,681 resolved before and all 1,681 resolve to the same entry after.
  - `record.py check` has 0 failures.
  - `check-index.sh` exits 0.

**Built differently from the review**
- **Pointer words** are kept and refreshed on a retitle, and check fails on stale words, as your brief says. Pointers changed by a retitle or a merge get no block of their own. `check --base` accepts them because they are named in the retitled or merged entry's block.
- **Pointer form:** conversions write `F-n, "words"`, matching the old `FACTS, "..."` and `PATH, "HEADING"` citation style. Where the old citation had a parenthesis they write `F-n ("...")`. Both forms are read. A word run may skip words with `...`.
- **Check rule 1** fails only on a missing number, not on a missing bold title. 47 FACTS entries have no bold title, so requiring one would have failed the numbering; they are reported instead.
- **Apply moves are explicit.** A heading places new entries only. An existing entry under a heading that is neither its own section nor the `##` above it is refused, and a `move` line moves it. A silent move risks POSITIONS entries landing in the wrong section, because `facts-extract.sh` prints them under their `##` heading.
- **`merge` takes FILE as optional.** The kind names the section moved to (`moved to "S"`); the target of a merge gets `F-n merged in`.
- **`check --base` refuses a pre-numbering commit** and points to `record-number.py --verify`.
- **Wider citation search:** the conversion also catches list citations (`POSITIONS, "A" and "B"`) and five bare whole titles inside POSITIONS, such as ("The judge's rulings."). A title query also accepts words ending in an ellipsis.
- **Size:** `record.py` is about 1,240 lines against the review's estimate of 450.

**Left for you or the coordinator**
- **Pointers by position:** about 14 are left in the record and will break when the consolidation moves lines, for example "the next entry" or "the VM entry above". They are in FACTS lines 12, 45, 53, 61, 81, 102, 180, 200 (twice), 201 and 210, and POSITIONS lines 50 and 76.
- **Sentences the numbering made untrue**, which I did not edit:
  - the header comments of `FACTS.md` and `POSITIONS.md`, which say the history keeps every earlier text by date and that entries are cited by bold title;
  - P-130, the review's decision 1;
  - `INDEX.md` lines 148 and 149;
  - the coordinator skill's `roles-and-records.md:32` (uses `check-verbatim.py`);
  - `fortress-repo` `records.md:37`.
- **`check-verbatim.py`** is left in the tree.
- **Untitled entries' titles shift:** the title of an entry without a bold title can change when a sentence is appended, and the tool then treats it as a retitle. Giving those entries bold titles in the consolidation ends this.
- **Report sections that don't resolve:** check reports three, cited by F-21, F-74 and F-201.
